title: SIEM export schema evolution & backwards compatibility checklist
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures the compatibility policy, checklist, and practical test vectors for evolving SIEM export envelopes (audit logs, RBAC v2 changes, evidence automation payloads) while preserving customer integrations with Splunk/Datadog/Azure Sentinel. It is intended for security engineering, connector owners, and professional services engineers who manage customer onboarding and migrations.

Scope:
- All outbound SIEM export envelopes produced by Redwood audit/evidence pipelines (hosted and dedicated).
- Connector adapters for Splunk HEC, Datadog HTTP intake, and Azure Sentinel connector.
- Schema changes that affect field names, types, envelope wrappers, and top-level routing metadata.
- Migration guidance for customers relying on field-level contract semantics (tenant routing, identity fields, retention markers).

Principles and policy summary:
1) Semantic versioning for SIEM envelopes: major.minor.patch. Backwards incompatible changes require a major version bump and a 90-day deprecation window and coordinated customer migration plan.
2) Default behavior: The platform will continue emitting the last stable major version (v1) for all customers until opt-in to a v2 sealed contract (config flag per-customer).
3) Additive-only by default: new optional fields are safe; changing types, removing fields, or renaming requires major version.
4) Envelope envelope: Keep a thin, consistent wrapper containing metadata used by connectors. Any change to wrapper keys (e.g., routing, tenant_id) is major.
5) Evidence references: evidence automation attachments MUST remain reference-based (evidence_refs) rather than inlining binary content as fields.

Common envelope top-level (v1 reference):
- envelope_version: string ("v1")
- produced_at: integer (ms since epoch)
- tenant_id: string
- route_hint: string (optional, used for multi-tenant routing)
- event_type: string (audit_event | rbac_change | evidence_generated | system_alert)
- severity: string (info|warning|error|critical)
- payload: object (consumer-facing event body; provider adapters may flatten to top-level fields)
- request_id: string
- trace_id: string (optional)

Note: We include the above as the canonical contract for the stable v1 stream. Connectors should map payload fields into target SIEM fields but must not discard envelope metadata.

Checklist for a proposed schema change (owners must complete before merge):
- [ ] Change classification: additive | breaking | behavioral (e.g., different timezone formatting).
- [ ] Back-compat statement: will old clients break? If yes, prepare major-version path.
- [ ] Customer impact analysis: list customers that consume the fields directly (PLS export usage logs + onboarding tickets).
- [ ] Connector mapping update: Splunk props/transforms, Datadog attribute mapping, Sentinel Kusto ingestion mapping.
- [ ] Regression test vectors: example messages for v1 and v2.
- [ ] Evidence automation impact: ensure evidence_refs schema remains stable and retention metadata preserved.
- [ ] RBAC v2 audit correlation: verify rbac_changes include before/after snapshots and user context fields (actor_id, actor_email).
- [ ] Docs + release notes: human readable migration steps, change rationale, sample queries for common SIEM (Splunk/Datadog/Sentinel).
- [ ] Migration toggle: server-side per-customer opt-in flag and rollback plan.
- [ ] QA plan: end-to-end test into staging Splunk/Datadog/Sentinel instances, performance regression testing for high-throughput exports.

Connector-specific guidance (high level):
- Splunk HEC: maintain host/source/sourcetype mappings. If new top-level keys are added, include them as fields prefixed with 'rw_' by default (e.g. rw_event_type). Avoid changing sourcetype semantics; instead create new sourcetype for major version (e.g. redwood:siem:v2).
- Datadog: map envelope metadata to datadog attributes (tags for tenant_id, event_type). Datadog's attribute size limits mean large payloads must be sent as indexed events with evidence_refs pointing to object storage, not as tags.
- Azure Sentinel: update the Kusto ingestion schema when introducing new top-level fields. Keep event_timestamp normalized to ISO8601 and provide produced_at_ms in the envelope for deterministic joins.

Migration patterns and customer playbooks:
1) Soft opt-in: create per-customer toggle in Console -> Integrations -> SIEM Export -> Schema version. Customers can enable v2 for a subset of tenants; the platform will simultaneously emit v1 and v2 for that customer for 7 days before switching to single-stream v2 (configurable).
2) Canary rollout: For high-volume customers, run a canary route (5% sample to the new schema path) and validate queries and dashboards before full roll out.
3) Fallback: If downstream errors are observed (HTTP 4xx/5xx, ingestion failures), automatically revert to v1 and create an incident with professional services assigned.

Test vectors (examples to include in test suite):
- v1 example: audit event for RBAC role assignment
  produced_at: 1700000000000
  envelope_version: v1
  tenant_id: corp-123
  event_type: rbac_change
  payload.summary: "role assignment"
  payload.detail: "user u-42 added to role infra-admin"
  request_id: r-abc-123

- v2 proposed example (additive change + normalized actor context):
  produced_at: 1700000001000
  envelope_version: v2
  tenant_id: corp-123
  event_type: rbac_change
  actor: { actor_id: "u-42", actor_email: "maria@example.com", actor_ip: "198.51.100.12" }
  payload: { change_set: [{type: "role_add", role: "infra-admin", target_user: "u-42"}], comment: "automated invite" }
  evidence_refs: ["s3://rw-evidence/2024/11/.." ]
  request_id: r-abc-124

(Tests should validate that connectors flatten actor.* properly or preserve nested actor JSON as 'rw_actor' depending on customer preference).

Release notes template (must be included with any major/minor change):
- change_summary: 1-2 line summary
- impacted_customers: list
- recommended_action: steps customers must take (query changes, dashboard edits)
- timeline: opt-in dates, mandatory cutover date (if any)
- rollback_instructions: how to revert to previous schema via Console toggle or API

Operational metrics to collect during rollout:
- drop_rate: percentage of exported events that failed mapping/ingestion per connector (monitor per-tenant).
- size_delta: change in average event size after schema change.
- query_failures: increase in saved-query failures for known dashboards (tracked via customer support tickets).

Customer contract paragraph (for outbound-facing docs):
"Redwood guarantees that SIEM export will maintain a stable v1 contract for a minimum of 90 days after announcing any incompatible schema change. Customers will be given a per-tenant opt-in to preview and test new schema versions. Redwood's professional services team will provide migration assistance as part of Dedicated and Private engagements. See migration playbook and contact ps@redwood.ai for enablement."

Operational runbook for connector engineers (short):
- Preflight: run automated schema-compat tests, run mapping scripts against customer's indexed sample from staging.
- Deploy: update connector mapping code and toggle feature flag to emit dual versions.
- Monitor: 24/7 on-call for first 72 hours, monitor drop_rate and ingestion errors.
- Rollback: toggle opt-in off; if rollback fails, pause export at router and switch to queued export from archive for critical customers.

Open questions and followups (owner: Maya Chen):
- What should the official deprecation window be for minor-but-breaking behavioral changes? Proposal: 90 days for major, 30 days for behavior-only changes with documented migration steps.
- Do we provide a managed mapping layer that rewrites v2 -> v1 for customers that cannot upgrade? (cost analysis required).
- Formalize test harness integrations with vendor-hosted Splunk/Datadog/Sentinel sandboxes (next steps: PS / QA ticket creation).

Appendix: Helpful queries and mappings (short pointers):
- Splunk: use sourcetype=redwood:siem:v1 to find legacy; search for rw_event_type if using prefixed fields.
- Datadog: recommended tags: tenant_id:<id>, event_type:<type>, severity:<level>. Use event streams for large payloads; avoid making evidence_refs tags.
- Sentinel: create ingestion mapping table mapping envelope fields to columns; index produced_at as datetime and keep produced_at_ms for exact ordering.

Contact: Maya Chen (maya@redwood.ai) — reach out with proposed schema diffs, sample payloads, customer lists for impact analysis.
